messages:
Alex: Ran an nsys capture on dedicated-8g last night (8k seq, batcher=adaptive). Timeline shows a ~4ms host->device memcpy on stream5 that appears to serialize subsequent kernels on stream5 while stream7 still runs. nvtx shows kernels: kv_prefetch, merged_attn_fwd, mv_mul. attaching trace: http://perf/redwood/3098765432/trace.nsys

Priya: can you paste the nsys command and a tiny timeline snippet? are those memcpy ops cuMemcpyHtoD or some driver ghost-copy?

Alex: command: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/run3098 --sample=cpu --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./run_infer.sh --seq 8192`
Timeline text snippet:
```
T=0us   stream5: cuMemcpyHtoD         4.1ms
T=4.2ms stream5: merged_attn_fwd_kernel 0.6ms
T=4.9ms stream7: mv_mul_kernel        0.4ms
T=5.3ms stream5: kv_prefetch_kernel   0.2ms
```

Marco: hmm looks like hostcopy isn't being overlapped. are we allocating staging buffer with pinned memory? if you use `cudaMemcpyAsync` from pageable memory the driver may do a ghost copy that serializes. check allocation path. also what's stream priority?

Alex: i grepped the path: host staging uses `malloc` + `cudaMemcpyAsync(..., stream)` — so pageable host memory. We never pinned for large batches. that explains the long cuMemcpyHtoD.

Priya: confirmed — pageable async copies can still block other work. short-term: use `cudaMallocHost` (pinned), or register the buffer with `cudaHostRegister`, or move to `cudaMemcpyAsync` from pinned pool. also try `cudaMemcpyAsync` paired with `cudaStreamAttachMemAsync` when using unified memory/prefetch. and consider stream priorities (`cudaStreamCreateWithPriority`) so critical kernels run on high-prio streams.

Alex: i'm going to re-run with `cudaMallocHost` for staging and repro. also will try `cudaStreamCreateWithPriority(NULL, high)` for prefetch kernels.

perf-bot: :warning: perf-alert detected. kv_prefetch p95 increased +18% between builds 2026-03-14 -> 2026-03-17. See alert: http://perf/redwood/alerts/452

Marco: another angle — last rollout changed merged_attn_fwd tiling (new kernel variant). could be higher register pressure / different occupancy making overlap behavior worse. check compile flags and kernel selection logs.

Alex: plan: (1) small microbenchmark reproducer (2) re-run nsys with only nvtx + cudaApi to reduce noise (3) try pinned vs pageable, and check `cuMemcpyHtoD` durations (4) record CPU `perf` to see sched wakeups aligning with memcpy completions. anyone want to pair? free for 30m.

Priya: i'll join. bring perfetto if you want the flame view; also run `perf record -g -- sleep 10` on the host during the trace to inspect `sched_wakeup` / `throttled` events. sometimes kernel runtime gets delayed by CPU preemption around the memcpy syscall.

Alex: quick follow-up after 68s: re-run with pinned host buffers — cuMemcpyHtoD drops to ~0.12ms and merged_attn_fwd now runs concurrently on stream7. new trace: http://perf/redwood/3098765432/trace_pinned.nsys

Priya: nice. let's add a small regression test that asserts large-batch host staging uses pinned buffers and add a note to batching-heuristics docs.

Marco: also consider a runtime defensive: if staging buffer not pinned and size > 64KB then warn and fallback to pre-allocated pinned pool. low-cost safety net.

Alex: filing issue: https://redwood.infer/issue/RT-721 (includes traces, command lines, and quick repro).

Priya: :thumbsup:
